bull_bear.body: Debt-free balance sheet with $235M+ cash; Strong cash conversion (OCF/EBITDA 76% LTM); No dividends/buybacks mentioned; Focus on organic growth and selective tuck-in acquisitions (CyberSolve integration ongoing).
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: GSE consolidation deal still WIP (70bps full-year headwind assumed); AI productivity dampener on existing scope (20-40% reduction potential); Q1 seasonality exacerbated by calendar and client budget delays; Execution risk on large rebadging deals impacting H1 margins; Macro spottiness in Consumer & Manufacturing.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Candid on short-term headwinds (calendar, GSE cuts, AI dampener) but highly confident on long-term AI opportunity and deal pipeline quality; Emphasized 'first-mover' status in AI offerings; Conservative guidance to ensure deliverability.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Management explicitly baked in a 'downside case' for the pending GSE consolidation deal despite being incumbent; The $25M earnout reversal on Softcrylic indicates aggressive initial targets missed due to macro/bankruptcy of two software clients; New 'Zero License' service aims to actively help clients exit SaaS contracts, creating a counter-intuitive revenue model based on replacement rather than license resale.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Closing cash balance as of 30th Jun 2026 of USD 176 Mn (includes restricted and MF investments, at exchange rate 94.66); balance sheet cash and cash equivalents INR 16,596 Mn vs INR 21,324 Mn at Dec-25.
- Dividend paid of INR 5,181 Mn in H1CY26 versus INR 3,494 Mn in H1CY25 — the largest single financing outflow, against H1CY26 OCF of INR 3,928 Mn.
- Balance sheet is acquisition-heavy: goodwill of INR 37,710 Mn (Jun-26) vs INR 35,768 Mn (Dec-25) against total assets of INR 1,15,757 Mn, with contingent consideration of INR 5,135 Mn still outstanding (INR 6,354 Mn at Dec-25).
- Working capital is absorbing cash: trade receivables and unbilled revenue rose to INR 32,845 Mn (Jun-26) from INR 25,431 Mn (Dec-25); changes in working capital were a INR (5,336) Mn drag in H1CY26.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: Financial Services strongest vertical (sequential & YoY growth); Banking 3rd straight quarter of strong growth; H&I max new logo traction; M&C bottoming out, back to green YoY; HTPS split into Professional Services (trailing, stabilizing) and new TPP vertical (Tech, Products, Platforms); GTT healthy YoY growth; APAC trailing but expected turnaround in CY26.

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Describes itself as a global digital and technology services company with AI at its core, serving 30+ of the Fortune 500 with a team of 34,506 employees across 30+ countries.
- Partnership strategy is explicitly three-layered: "FOUNDATION — Anthropic (Claude)", "DOMAIN — E.g., Articul8, Mistral ModelMesh/Foundry, vertical-tuned models" and "CONTEXT — E.g., Workfabric", with its own vertical products/platforms (Agentverse, Tensai, RapidX, Amaze) sitting above; the stated thesis is that "Every enterprise will have access to the same frontier models. Differentiation comes from what sits above them — vertical depth and client-specific context."
- Revenue is spread across seven verticals (Q2CY26 INR mix: Financial Services 28.7%, Healthcare & Insurance 23.1%, Manufacturing & Consumer 16.0%, Professional Services 13.8%, Banking 9.0%, Travel & Transportation 7.2%, Technology/Products & Platforms 2.1%) and three geographies (Americas 73.6%, Europe 19.9%, Asia Pacific 6.5%).
- Client concentration has eased over the LTM: Top 5 customers 25.3% (vs 25.8% LTM Q2CY25), Top 10 35.7% (vs 36.6%) and Top 20 48.7% (vs 50.1%), while $1 Mn+ clients rose to 206 from 197.
- Deal slate cited spans a leading global clinical research company (CRM transformation), ANZ Financial Services (Digital ITO), a Capital Market Institution (Zero License), a German biotechnology company (AI for Business) and a UK music copyright organization (Legacy Modernization).
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Guidance cut] "our pathway to 7.6% has narrowed, especially because of delay in deal ramp and worsening macro. We are reducing our guidance to a range of 6-7%, including 50 bps from the CP rebadging deal. This implies a 2.7% CQGR at mid-point which we are confident of delivering." EBIT margin guidance is reiterated at 13.0%–14.0%.
- [Vertical outlook CY26] "H&I, Banking and M&C are expected to lead the growth for CY26; PS and FS to follow; T&T is expected to lag due to macro."
- [Vendor consolidation] "Consolidation deal in another Top 15 customer, down to 3 strategic vendors", with increased deal momentum in >$10 Mn legacy modernization programs.
- [Restatement] Prior-period vertical and geography numbers "have been restated to reflect internal organization realignment of customers to verticals and geographies", so vertical/geo history is not on a like-for-like basis.
- [Recognition] S&P Global Sustainability Yearbook 2026 (top 10% of industry in the 2025 CSA), Top 25 Most Valuable IT Brands globally by Brand Finance, Client Champion in the 2025 ISG Star of Excellence Awards, and multiple ISG Provider Lens leader placements (Snowflake, Microsoft/Azure, SAP S/4HANA midmarket, GCC design & setup, AI-ready infrastructure UK).
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: Q4 Normalized margin 15.4% (-210bps QoQ): Forex -20bps, Calendar -60bps, Utilization -60bps, Merit hikes -90bps. CY26 EBIT margin guide 13-14%: Pressured in H1 by rebadging (3 deals) and ramp-up costs, recovering in H2 to exceed current year levels. Labor code change adds ~20bps annual headwind.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue growth >7.6% (CY26) with acceleration post-Q1; EBIT margin 13-14% for CY26 (H1 depressed by rebadging/ramp-ups, H2 recovery); Order inflow strong with pipeline >$4B; Capex not explicitly quantified but focused on capacity building for deal ramp-ups.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Pipeline crossed $4B for first time; Key wins: Large Big Tech consolidation deal (right to hunt/RFPs, no predefined book), Global largest pet insurer (end-to-end tech run), Large insurance Guidewire modernization, Global CRO (agentic AI), World's largest casual dining holding co, Large Asian tech services GCC deal, Large PBM product development.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: AI-for-Business replacing SaaS licenses (Zero License offering); Legacy modernization at scale (2-3 large completions expected); Private Markets vertical launch (new CPO hired); GCC expansion via SMC acquisition; Agentic AI in clinical research and IT operations.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Hexaware reported a sequential revenue decline driven by seasonal furloughs, calendar effects, and a specific GSE budget cut, masking robust underlying deal wins including a major Big Tech consolidation opportunity. While Q1 FY27 faces margin compression from rebadging and utilization ramp-ups, the company guides for full-year growth acceleration above 7.6% as new AI-enabled services and large deal ramp-ups materialize in H2.

open.item: The Hyderabad delivery center, which became operational in February 2026, is expected to grow to more than 500 employees through the year.

Committed to net zero emissions by 2040, with near-term and long-term targets approved by the Science Based Targets initiative (SBTi), to be achieved through clean energy, sustainable infrastructure and smart resource management.
Announced plans for a major new delivery center in Birmingham, UK, to strengthen presence in the Middle East and Europe (following the Cairo, Egypt center that has already opened).

risks.note: Economic uncertainty can slow client decision-making and push out timelines for discretionary technology projects even when business cases are strong.
risks.risk: Macro uncertainty and longer decision cycles

risks.note: Clients seeking more value at lower cost and reducing the number of vendors they work with increases competitive intensity and makes pricing discussions more challenging.

A significant proportion of executives report bringing previously outsourced work back in-house; expanded client GCCs and internal AI/engineering teams can shift scope away from external providers like Hexaware.
As AI becomes embedded in delivery, errors or weak controls in AI systems can create operational, reputational or regulatory issues, requiring ongoing investment in governance and quality.
Data protection and AI-related regulations continue to evolve; combined with rising cyber threats, this raises the bar on security capabilities, compliance monitoring and third-party risk management.
Demand for skills in AI, cloud, security and modern engineering remains high; sustained reskilling, upskilling and retention are required to keep pace with client needs.
The Americas contributed 75.3% of revenue share versus 19% Europe and 5.8% Asia-Pacific, leaving the business heavily exposed to demand and macro conditions in a single region.
risks.risk: Geographic revenue concentration in the Americas

risks.note: Large global IT services firms, specialist boutiques, hyperscalers, platform vendors and clients' own GCCs all compete for similar technology budgets, with clients evaluating not just capability but who takes accountability for outcomes.
